final_recommendation: The room failed to converge on an operational underwriting framework. Despite locking a standardized template with quarterly audits, Big Four attestation requirements, and AI-bypass testing mandates, the group could not resolve critical execution gaps: validation capacity, E&O coverage for internal review work, correlated accumulation risk from shared auditor methodologies, and the existing AT1 litigation tail reserve assumptions. The meeting terminated without binding authority.
minority_objections: AI agent analyst repeatedly challenged whether attestation review constituted actual re-testing of bypass scenarios or merely documentation compliance theater
Reinsurance manager flagged that binding thirty policies on a single auditor's methodology without independent validation creates correlated accumulation across the cohort
Emerging risk lead questioned whether internal validation without external audit oversight creates single-point failure risk
key_conflicts: Validation depth: whether reviewers would re-execute bypass tests against live systems or merely spot-check auditor documentation
E&O coverage gap: whether the insurer's validation work was covered by separate E&O or would fall back to client D&O policies, creating liability circularity
Capacity vs. discipline: whether six reviewers could validate thirty attestations in parallel without queue collapse forcing discretionary overrides
Existing tail quantification: whether the 2025 AT1 ruling shifted reserve assumptions from 'settlement likely' to '4-6 year full recovery risk'
key_concessions: Financial lines underwriter agreed to hard-stop binding conditions with zero override authority
D&O specialist accepted 12-month auditor E&O recovery window as sufficient if testing-scope attestation was documented
E&O specialist agreed to Big Four rotation mandate (no single auditor >40% of book) to isolate contagion
All parties accepted that self-reported control attestations required 25% pricing loading
red_lines: No binding without Big Four third-party attestation filed and countersigned by controls team
Material weakness discovery triggers automatic coverage suspension with no discretionary override
Auditor E&O indemnity capped at 12 months post-opinion-failure, non-negotiable
If staffing (six reviewers) not confirmed by Monday EOD, $5M D&O / $2M E&O sublimit auto-triggers with volume cap
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: The room never quantified the existing $115M AT1 settlement tail or modeled how the 2025 'unlawful write-off' ruling changes defense cost reserves for directors
Client flight risk during the 5-day attestation review window was not discussed—no analysis of competitive shopping behavior if binding delays
Regulatory compression (the 48-hour UBS-Credit Suisse forced merger) was mentioned in context but never developed into a speed-of-crisis underwriting variable
Reputational contagion across the sector (one KPMG methodology failure triggering thirty simultaneous claims) was flagged but not modeled or priced
downstream_risk_variables: Quarterly control audit mandate with material-weakness suspension trigger
Big Four attestation requirement with testing-scope documentation and 12-month E&O indemnity
AI-agent bypass testing as mandatory audit scope (guardrail validation, not just deployment sign-off)
Auditor rotation requirement (no single firm >40% of bound book)
Hard-stop binding gate: no coverage effective until controls team countersigns attestation
Staffing-contingent sublimit: $5M D&O / $2M E&O if six-reviewer capacity not confirmed
15-20% pricing floor for policies without board-attestation warranties
uncertainty_notes: The room could not resolve whether internal validation of auditor work constitutes actual re-testing or documentation review, creating unquantified correlated accumulation risk. E&O coverage for the insurer's own validation team remains undefined. The existing AT1 litigation tail reserve assumption ('unlikely recovery' vs. '4-6 year full recovery risk') was disputed but not reconciled. Binding capacity under load (thirty clients in week two) was asserted but not proven.
